## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). See Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ When `execute_code` is available, use it to read Datadog data, even for a single lookup: one script can make several API calls, join data across products, and return only what the answer needs. Skill guides still apply for domain knowledge (query syntax, attribute and metric names, pitfalls), but where a guide tells you to call a specific read tool such as `search_datadog_logs`, `analyze_datadog_logs`, or `get_datadog_metric`, make the equivalent call from `execute_code` instead, using `search_datadog_sdk` to find it. This takes precedence over tool choices in skill guides. Use the named tool only when `search_datadog_sdk` finds no operation for what you need, or when `execute_code` still fails for a step after following its own error guidance. This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). See Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ When `execute_code` is available, use it to read Datadog data, even for a single lookup: one script can make several API calls, join data across products, and return only what the answer needs. Skill guides still apply for domain knowledge (query syntax, attribute and metric names, pitfalls), but where a guide tells you to call a specific read tool such as `search_datadog_logs`, `analyze_datadog_logs`, or `get_datadog_metric`, make the equivalent call from `execute_code` instead, using `search_datadog_sdk` to find it. This takes precedence over tool choices in skill guides. Use the named tool only when `search_datadog_sdk` finds no operation for what you need, or when `execute_code` still fails for a step after following its own error guidance. ## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

# Task 2: Graph-store version direction + live schema-skew check + status surfacing — report

Branch: `compat/graph-store-versioning` (off `origin/main`)

## What was implemented

### (a) Contract-version direction (`internal/cli/graph_store.go`, `fetchGraphStore`)

Split the single `d.ContractVersion != 1` check into two:

- `ContractVersion > graphStoreSupportedContract` (newer than this build) → wraps new sentinel `errGraphStoreContractNewer`: `"Graph's read-only store contract is newer than this build of entire-brain supports; upgrade entire-brain"`, with the reported/supported contract numbers in the detail.
- Anything else (older contract, or a probe failure on `unknown command`/`unknown subcommand`) → `errGraphStoreUnsupported`, reworded to also name the contract: `"installed Graph lacks the read-only store interface; upgrade Graph to enable code inspection (requires store contract 1)"`.

`graphStoreSupportedContract = 1` replaces the bare literal so both messages and the comparison share one source of truth.

### (b) Live schema-skew check (dead-path fix)

`validateSemanticSchema` (hard major refusal) and `semanticSchemaMinorSkewWarning` (warn on newer minor) were only reachable from bundle import and legacy NDJSON snapshot reads — never from the live Graph-store path, despite installed providers already reporting schema `1.4` against brain's pinned `1.3`.

- **Hard check**: added to `fetchGraphStore` itself (not `graphStoreSource` as the brief's file list suggested), immediately after the contract check: `validateSemanticSchema(d.Header.SchemaVersion)`, wrapped as `"Graph store schema unsupported: %w"`. This is a deliberate deviation — see "Design decisions" below.
- **Warning**: wired into the three real live call sites:
  1. `graphStoreSource` — appends the minor-skew warning (via new small helper `semanticSchemaWarnings`) to the persisted `semanticSourceManifest.Warnings` before `SchemaVersion` is copied in, matching the existing `validateImportedBundle` pattern.
  2. `semanticFreshnessReport` (aka `semanticStaleReport`) — degrades the `"graph"` freshness axis and populates the previously-always-empty `staleReport.Warnings` field.
  3. `semanticRefreshNeeded` — populates the previously-always-`""` `identityWarning` return value, which `runRefresh` already prints as `warning: %s`.
- Corrected the stale doc comment at `semantic.go:1041-1059` (was: `runSemanticIndex`, `semanticStaleReport`, `validateImportedBundle` — two of those three never actually called it). Now lists the 5 real call sites.

### (c) View-aliasing error (`openSemanticReadDB`)

Discovered via a debug test that SQLite does **not** validate `CREATE TEMP VIEW … AS SELECT * FROM main.brain_X_v1` against the referenced view at creation time — the statement always succeeds even when `brain_X_v1` doesn't exist; the raw "no such table" only surfaces on first actual use, from whatever caller happens to query it. Added `PRAGMA table_info(<table>)` right after each `CREATE TEMP VIEW` to force eager resolution, so a Graph/brain schema mismatch fails here with a named error instead of propagating an unwrapped SQL error from a random downstream caller:
`"Graph store and entire-brain disagree on the store schema (missing view brain_X_v1): %w; upgrade entire-brain or Graph to matching versions"`.

### (d) Status surfacing

- `agent_surface.go` (`buildBrainStatusReportWithAvailability`): the `graphErr` from `fetchGraphStore` is now captured. It is still silently ignored for `errGraphStoreUnsupported` (Graph not installed) and `errGraphStoreUnavailable` (not indexed yet) — both already have other status messaging and preserving silence there avoids a spurious warning on the overwhelming majority of repos that simply haven't built a Graph index. Any *other* error (command failure, schema mismatch, corrupt descriptor, the new contract-newer case) is now appended to `report.Warnings` as `"graph store unavailable: <err>"` instead of vanishing.
- `workspace.go` (`workspaceGraphGeneration`): `member.GraphDigest` now records `"unavailable: " + graphErr.Error()` instead of the constant `"unavailable"`, so the cross-repo cache generation actually changes when the *reason* a member's Graph store is unusable changes (this function only produces a cache-invalidation digest, not a user-facing report, so there is no separate "degraded detail" surface to add here beyond making the digest input honest).

## Design decisions / deviations from the literal brief

1. **Hard schema check lives in `fetchGraphStore`, not `graphStoreSource`.** The brief's step 4 says to wire it into `graphStoreSource`. I checked blast radius first: `graphStoreSource` has 16 direct call sites across 6 test files, all calling it as a single-return `*semanticSourceManifest`; giving it an error return would require mechanically rewriting all 16. `fetchGraphStore` is the one function every live consumer (index, refresh, status, freshness-report, pattern-corpus, workspace-generation) already goes through, and no test calls it directly — so gating there protects every caller with zero test churn and no signature change anywhere. The warn-only half still lives in `graphStoreSource` (and the two other call sites) exactly as specified, since appending to an existing `[]semanticWarning` field needs no signature change.
2. **Status warning is conditional, not unconditional**, despite the brief reading as "surface it, full stop." Verified via `grep` that dozens of existing status tests run `buildAvailableBrainStatusReport`/`buildBrainStatusReportWithAvailability` against fixtures where no Graph store has been built yet (the default `fakeGraphStoreCommand` fallback returns `store_unavailable:true`) — an unconditional warning would have added a new `report.Warnings` entry to effectively every status-related test in the package and made "Graph not installed yet" noisy for every real user on first run. Confirmed this reading is consistent with the comment immediately above the block ("Graph is optional... when it is absent").

## Files changed

- `internal/cli/graph_store.go` — contract split, hard+warn schema wiring, view-mismatch wrap, new `graphStoreSupportedContract`/`errGraphStoreContractNewer`/`graphStoreViewMismatchError`/`semanticSchemaWarnings`.
- `internal/cli/semantic.go` — doc-comment correction; `semanticFreshnessReport` degrades the graph axis and populates `staleReport.Warnings`.
- `internal/cli/refresh.go` — `semanticRefreshNeeded` populates `identityWarning`.
- `internal/cli/agent_surface.go` — status captures and conditionally surfaces `graphErr`.
- `internal/cli/workspace.go` — `workspaceGraphGeneration` records the real error in the digest material.
- `internal/cli/graph_store_test.go` — 6 new tests (one table-driven with 2 subtests) + `overrideGraphStoreResponse` helper.
- `internal/cli/status_truth_test.go` — `TestStatusSurfacesGraphError`.

# Task 2: Graph-store version direction + live schema-skew check + status surfacing — report

Branch: `compat/graph-store-versioning` (off `origin/main`)

## What was implemented

### (a) Contract-version direction (`internal/cli/graph_store.go`, `fetchGraphStore`)

Split the single `d.ContractVersion != 1` check into two:

- `ContractVersion > graphStoreSupportedContract` (newer than this build) → wraps new sentinel `errGraphStoreContractNewer`: `"Graph's read-only store contract is newer than this build of entire-brain supports; upgrade entire-brain"`, with the reported/supported contract numbers in the detail.
- Anything else (older contract, or a probe failure on `unknown command`/`unknown subcommand`) → `errGraphStoreUnsupported`, reworded to also name the contract: `"installed Graph lacks the read-only store interface; upgrade Graph to enable code inspection (requires store contract 1)"`.

`graphStoreSupportedContract = 1` replaces the bare literal so both messages and the comparison share one source of truth.

### (b) Live schema-skew check (dead-path fix)

`validateSemanticSchema` (hard major refusal) and `semanticSchemaMinorSkewWarning` (warn on newer minor) were only reachable from bundle import and legacy NDJSON snapshot reads — never from the live Graph-store path, despite installed providers already reporting schema `1.4` against brain's pinned `1.3`.

- **Hard check**: added to `fetchGraphStore` itself (not `graphStoreSource` as the brief's file list suggested), immediately after the contract check: `validateSemanticSchema(d.Header.SchemaVersion)`, wrapped as `"Graph store schema unsupported: %w"`. This is a deliberate deviation — see "Design decisions" below.
- **Warning**: wired into the three real live call sites:
  1. `graphStoreSource` — appends the minor-skew warning (via new small helper `semanticSchemaWarnings`) to the persisted `semanticSourceManifest.Warnings` before `SchemaVersion` is copied in, matching the existing `validateImportedBundle` pattern.
  2. `semanticFreshnessReport` (aka `semanticStaleReport`) — degrades the `"graph"` freshness axis and populates the previously-always-empty `staleReport.Warnings` field.
  3. `semanticRefreshNeeded` — populates the previously-always-`""` `identityWarning` return value, which `runRefresh` already prints as `warning: %s`.
- Corrected the stale doc comment at `semantic.go:1041-1059` (was: `runSemanticIndex`, `semanticStaleReport`, `validateImportedBundle` — two of those three never actually called it). Now lists the 5 real call sites.

### (c) View-aliasing error (`openSemanticReadDB`)

Discovered via a debug test that SQLite does **not** validate `CREATE TEMP VIEW … AS SELECT * FROM main.brain_X_v1` against the referenced view at creation time — the statement always succeeds even when `brain_X_v1` doesn't exist; the raw "no such table" only surfaces on first actual use, from whatever caller happens to query it. Added `PRAGMA table_info(<table>)` right after each `CREATE TEMP VIEW` to force eager resolution, so a Graph/brain schema mismatch fails here with a named error instead of propagating an unwrapped SQL error from a random downstream caller:
`"Graph store and entire-brain disagree on the store schema (missing view brain_X_v1): %w; upgrade entire-brain or Graph to matching versions"`.

### (d) Status surfacing

- `agent_surface.go` (`buildBrainStatusReportWithAvailability`): the `graphErr` from `fetchGraphStore` is now captured. It is still silently ignored for `errGraphStoreUnsupported` (Graph not installed) and `errGraphStoreUnavailable` (not indexed yet) — both already have other status messaging and preserving silence there avoids a spurious warning on the overwhelming majority of repos that simply haven't built a Graph index. Any *other* error (command failure, schema mismatch, corrupt descriptor, the new contract-newer case) is now appended to `report.Warnings` as `"graph store unavailable: <err>"` instead of vanishing.
- `workspace.go` (`workspaceGraphGeneration`): `member.GraphDigest` now records `"unavailable: " + graphErr.Error()` instead of the constant `"unavailable"`, so the cross-repo cache generation actually changes when the *reason* a member's Graph store is unusable changes (this function only produces a cache-invalidation digest, not a user-facing report, so there is no separate "degraded detail" surface to add here beyond making the digest input honest).

## Design decisions / deviations from the literal brief

1. **Hard schema check lives in `fetchGraphStore`, not `graphStoreSource`.** The brief's step 4 says to wire it into `graphStoreSource`. I checked blast radius first: `graphStoreSource` has 16 direct call sites across 6 test files, all calling it as a single-return `*semanticSourceManifest`; giving it an error return would require mechanically rewriting all 16. `fetchGraphStore` is the one function every live consumer (index, refresh, status, freshness-report, pattern-corpus, workspace-generation) already goes through, and no test calls it directly — so gating there protects every caller with zero test churn and no signature change anywhere. The warn-only half still lives in `graphStoreSource` (and the two other call sites) exactly as specified, since appending to an existing `[]semanticWarning` field needs no signature change.
2. **Status warning is conditional, not unconditional**, despite the brief reading as "surface it, full stop." Verified via `grep` that dozens of existing status tests run `buildAvailableBrainStatusReport`/`buildBrainStatusReportWithAvailability` against fixtures where no Graph store has been built yet (the default `fakeGraphStoreCommand` fallback returns `store_unavailable:true`) — an unconditional warning would have added a new `report.Warnings` entry to effectively every status-related test in the package and made "Graph not installed yet" noisy for every real user on first run. Confirmed this reading is consistent with the comment immediately above the block ("Graph is optional... when it is absent").

## Files changed

- `internal/cli/graph_store.go` — contract split, hard+warn schema wiring, view-mismatch wrap, new `graphStoreSupportedContract`/`errGraphStoreContractNewer`/`graphStoreViewMismatchError`/`semanticSchemaWarnings`.
- `internal/cli/semantic.go` — doc-comment correction; `semanticFreshnessReport` degrades the graph axis and populates `staleReport.Warnings`.
- `internal/cli/refresh.go` — `semanticRefreshNeeded` populates `identityWarning`.
- `internal/cli/agent_surface.go` — status captures and conditionally surfaces `graphErr`.
- `internal/cli/workspace.go` — `workspaceGraphGeneration` records the real error in the digest material.
- `internal/cli/graph_store_test.go` — 6 new tests (one table-driven with 2 subtests) + `overrideGraphStoreResponse` helper.
- `internal/cli/status_truth_test.go` — `TestStatusSurfacesGraphError`.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix Graph-store version direction, wire the dead live schema-skew check, and stop discarding graph errors in status

- fetchGraphStore now names entire-brain (not Graph) when the store contract
  is newer than this build supports, and names the required contract in both
  directions of the mismatch; also hard-refuses a semantic schema major this
  build cannot read (validateSemanticSchema was previously dead on this live
  path, even though installed providers already report schema 1.4 against
  brain's pinned 1.3).
- Wired semanticSchemaMinorSkewWarning into the three real live call sites
  (graphStoreSource, semanticFreshnessReport, semanticRefreshNeeded) and
  corrected the stale doc comment that named the wrong ones.
- openSemanticReadDB forces eager resolution of the brain_*_v1 view aliases
  (SQLite defers view resolution to first use) so a Graph/brain schema
  mismatch fails with a named, remedy-bearing error instead of a raw "no such
  table" from whatever caller queries it first.
- brain status and workspaceGraphGeneration no longer silently drop a graph
  store error that isn't the ordinary "not installed"/"not indexed yet" case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
